title: Make every send thread honour a block within one message

blocks.text: This practice continues the previous one: `Store` now replaces the rules on every change, and send threads read them without a lock. Each send thread takes a batch of up to 5,000 queued messages at a time and hands the allowed ones to the mail transfer agent through a `Transport`.

When a partner domain asks the service to stop, the admin blocks it, and the partner expects the mail to stop within a message or two. The batch that was sending at the time must not finish the domain's queue first, and a sender that has been running since the morning must not keep the rules it started with.

Finish `sendAll(...)` of `Sender` in `src/main/java/practice/DeliveryRules.java`. A sender gets its rules from a `Supplier<Rules>`, which is `store::current` in production. When you're done, it sends each message the rules allow, in order, and returns how many it sent; a change to the rules applies from the next message on; and a message is never let through by one version's block list together with another version's size limit. About seven lines in total.
The tests change the rules from inside the transport, between two messages, and hand the sender suppliers that return a different version on every call.

cases.says: a batch sends, in order, the messages the rules allow and skips blocked domains and messages over their domain's size limit
a block made while a batch is being sent stops the batch's later messages to that domain
a change made after the sender was created applies to the batches it sends afterwards
the block check and the size check of one message use the same version of the rules, even when the rules change between them

origin.section: Settings Are One Immutable Snapshot, Replaced Whole and Read Once per Unit of Work

concepts: A replaced snapshot reaches a reader only when it reads the field again, so a reader reads it once per unit of work, never once per batch or per worker, and uses that one snapshot for every check of the unit.
